title: U.S. Expels Cuban Diplomat After Clash at U.N. General Assembly
dek: Secretary of State Marco Rubio ordered the expulsion of a Cuban diplomat accused of shoving and trying to assault a member of U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz's team during a heated U.N. debate.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The General Assembly hall at United Nations Headquarters in New York City

keyPoints: Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed an order expelling a Cuban diplomat, according to U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz, who said the man tried to intimidate a U.S. official.
The confrontation came on Tuesday during the General Assembly's annual debate on the U.S. embargo of Cuba, as Waltz was speaking against a resolution to end the restrictions.
Cuba's foreign minister, Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla, accused Waltz of lying; the Cuban government's account of the expulsion was not available in the reporting reviewed here.
body:
The United States has ordered the expulsion of a Cuban diplomat after a confrontation on the floor of the United Nations General Assembly, a clash that ended with the U.S. ambassador saying the man had tried to physically intimidate a member of his team.

## What happened

The exchange took place on Tuesday, during the General Assembly's annual debate on the decades-long U.S. embargo of Cuba. Ambassador Mike Waltz was speaking against a resolution that would end the restrictions when members of the Cuban delegation objected loudly, according to reports from Newsweek and WORLD. Cuba's foreign minister, Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla, approached the podium and argued that Waltz's speech violated the assembly's procedural rules. The meeting was briefly suspended.

Waltz, speaking on Fox News' Hannity on Tuesday night, said a Cuban first secretary had "shoved and tried to assault" a member of his team and that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had signed paperwork to expel him. "He's gone," Waltz said, adding that the diplomat would be on a plane to Havana within 24 hours. Newsweek reported that video of the confrontation was shared by Waltz on social media.

## The U.S. account

According to WORLD, the U.S. government did not publicly name the diplomat. Waltz's account, as reported by WORLD and Notus, is that Cuban delegates rushed the stage during his speech and that one of them tried to snatch a phone from a member of his staff who was filming. Waltz also said the United States would not tolerate any attempt to intimidate Americans on U.S. soil.

In his remarks, Waltz accused the Cuban government of enriching its leaders while ordinary Cubans suffered, pointing to luxury goods and a private island he said was associated with the ruling family. Rubio separately posted a satellite image of a private island south of Cuba and described it as the property of a corrupt regime, according to Newsweek.

## Cuba's position

Cuba's delegation rejected the U.S. characterization. Rodríguez Parrilla told the assembly that Waltz was "lying yet again" and called his remarks beneath the dignity of the forum. Cuba has argued in previous U.N. debates that the U.S. embargo, along with a recent blockade of shadow-fleet tankers carrying oil to the island, is choking its economy. The U.S. says Cuba's socialist policies are responsible for blackouts and shortages.

## What is not yet known

The reporting reviewed for this story does not identify the diplomat publicly, and it does not include a formal statement from Havana on the expulsion. Newsweek said it had contacted Waltz and Rodríguez for comment. Neither the State Department nor the Cuban government has published a written order or account in the sources cited here. Meridian will update this story if either government releases a formal statement or the expulsion is carried out publicly.
